subject: Literature
title: Nazi Book Burnings of 1933
description: A quick, practical guide to Nazi Book Burnings of 1933.

hook.text: On May 10, 1933, Nazi students burned over twenty-five thousand books in a single bonfire in Berlin.

buildup.text: They targeted works by Jewish, socialist, and pacifist authors including Einstein, Freud, Hemingway, and Helen Keller.

discovery.text: Heinrich Heine had written a century earlier: 'Where they burn books, they will ultimately burn people also.'

twist.text: Heine was Jewish, and his own books were among those thrown into the flames that night, fulfilling his own prophecy.

climax.text: The Nazi book burnings proved that the destruction of literature is often the first step toward the destruction of lives.

punchline.text: The prophet of book burning had his own books burned.

quiz.question: What is significant about Heinrich Heine's connection to the Nazi book burnings?
options: He predicted them a century earlier, and his own books were burned
He was the only author whose books survived
